paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: in this passage, the LORD gives His prophet a heavy word about what is coming, and then gives him a job to do. The prophet hears a dire vision and his body fills with anguish (Isaiah 21:2-3). Then the Lord says, "Go, post a lookout and have him report what he sees." (Isaiah 21:6). The Lord tells the prophet to set up the watch, and the watch brings back an answer (Isaiah 21:9).

Now look at that lookout. He doesn't get one exciting night. He says, "Day after day, my lord, I stand on the watchtower; night after night I stay at my post." (Isaiah 21:8). Watching is not glamorous work, and I know a little about waiting around for something to happen. But the waiting is what put him in place to hear the word, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon!" (Isaiah 21:9).

And that's why this matters to you, baker. Babylon looked big and the party looked fine, but the gods lying shattered on the ground show that nothing outside the LORD stands forever (Isaiah 21:9). The prophet says it plainly to his crushed people: this is what he heard "from the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel." (Isaiah 21:10). So stay at your post, keep your ovens ready, and trust the One who already knows how the story ends.
